mappings.notes: New all-flow target register directly addresses numerical workload-driven targets for every user/system/data flow. Full is limited to the checklist control statement, not all linked guidance.
AKS capacity planning addresses SKU, autoscale, addressing and failover. It does not establish workload-wide anticipation of seasonal/campaign/regulatory demand changes.
VM/disk selection addresses workload performance profiles and durability. It does not cover every workload service choice or platform-versus-custom implementation.
App Service targets, traces and baseline comparison implement consistent measurement for this service, not every workload component.
AKS autoscaler review addresses controlled per-pool scale and constraints, not the complete workload scale-unit and partitioning design.
Recurring production-like AKS tests exercise pod/node scale with measurable targets. Other workload components and full end-to-end business objectives remain outside this service control.
App Service load-test targets, baseline comparisons and fail/stop criteria cover a specific hosting scope; not all workload tests.
Blob SDKs, bounded concurrency and server-side copies address efficient code/platform use for storage clients, not all code and infrastructure.
Files access-pattern and metadata optimization addresses one data service; broader store, partition and index design remains uncovered.
OpenAI traffic prioritization distinguishes synchronous high-priority and asynchronous lower-priority work, but not an all-flow business-criticality and capacity-allocation process.

New operational-task budget explicitly covers lifecycle and routine scans, rotation, backups, database maintenance and deployments, with measurement and minimization of performance overhead. Full applies only to the checklist statement.

New performance triage plan covers responsibilities/communication, diagnosis, recovery verification and preventive runbook improvements. Full applies to the checklist statement, not every implementation in linked guidance.
ML infrastructure monitoring, review and action support ongoing optimization in that service. Database/network deterioration elsewhere remains outside its scope.
v2 maximum capacity/subnet headroom addresses the autoscaling branch; the catalog also describes high utilization and v1 manual scaling. No live Advisor finding or utilization is inferred.
IP-group/prefix rule reduction addresses network-rule processing pressure, but this corpus check does not establish the catalog's measured unique-source/destination limit condition.
The catalog names classic Microsoft.Network/frontdoors. Modern Front Door probe guidance is related, but different resource scope prevents counting this as full or partial type-specific coverage.
